audit.whatIsWrong: Three places told the player Spirit's Refuge blocks Twin Fang. Riot's text for Refuge blocks ATTACKS — Twin Fang is an ability and passes through the zone untouched. Miasma's grounding was also described as cancelling Shadow Dash mid-animation; grounding prevents the cast, it does not interrupt one already in flight.
audit.why: Standing in Refuge expecting to eat her poison DPS is how this lane is lost. The real answers to Twin Fang are range discipline and Grievous Wounds, since it heals her for a share of the damage.

edits.before: Cassiopeia owns levels 1-5 because her Noxious Blast (Q) poke outranges your Twilight Assault (Q) autos and she can freely proc Twin Fang (E) on any poison hit without stepping into Shadow Dash (E) range. Your job is to respect the Miasma (W) green cloud completely — she places it in your engage path to cancel your dash and ground you, so never walk into it. Farm safely from max range with the tip of Twilight Assault's empowered autos, use Spirit's Refuge (W) whenever she commits to a trade burst to block Twin Fang hits, and accept that she out-DPSes you in straight poke trades. The Ki Barrier shield from ability use buys small margins; use it by weaving Q casts to generate shields between her poke waves rather than hard-committing to all-ins she can ground and punish.
edits.after: Cassiopeia owns levels 1-5 because her Noxious Blast (Q) poke outranges your Twilight Assault (Q) autos and she can freely proc Twin Fang (E) on any poison hit without stepping into Shadow Dash (E) range. Your job is to respect the Miasma (W) green cloud completely — grounded inside it you cannot cast your dash at all, so never walk into it. Farm safely from max range with the tip of Twilight Assault's empowered autos, keep Spirit's Refuge (W) for her autos rather than her poison, because Twin Fang is a spell the zone never blocks, and accept that she out-DPSes you in straight poke trades. The Ki Barrier shield from ability use buys small margins; weave Q casts to generate shields between her poke waves rather than hard-committing to all-ins she can ground and punish.

edits.before: Level 6 is where the matchup tilts in your favour on the macro map even if the lane footprint stays even. Cassiopeia has no mobility and no answer to Stand United (R) — every time a fed ADC or jungler gets dove, you teleport in, absorb damage through the shield, and turn the fight. In lane at this stage, track her Miasma (W) cooldown aggressively: when it is down, Shadow Dash (E) is safe to throw — taunt her into a Twilight Assault (Q) trade with Spirit's Refuge (W) blocking her Twin Fang spam, and your Ki Barrier shield absorbs her follow-up. She will try to pre-position Miasma before you engage, so bait her W placement by faking a walk-in, then dash the gap once it is deployed and on cooldown. Never walk into Petrifying Gaze (R) range while facing her — approach from the side or behind so even a landed R only slows you rather than stunning.
edits.after: Level 6 is where the matchup tilts in your favour on the macro map even if the lane footprint stays even. Cassiopeia has no mobility and no answer to Stand United (R) — every time a fed ADC or jungler gets dove, you teleport in, absorb damage through the shield, and turn the fight. In lane at this stage, track her Miasma (W) cooldown aggressively: when it is down, Shadow Dash (E) is safe to throw — taunt her into a Twilight Assault (Q) trade while Spirit's Refuge blocks her autos, though Twin Fang is a spell and still lands, and Ki Barrier absorbs the follow-up. She will try to pre-position Miasma before you engage, so bait the W by faking a walk-in, then dash once it is spent. Never face Petrifying Gaze (R) — the stun cancels Stand United mid-channel, so approach from the side where it only slows.

edits.before: That is Cassiopeia's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Twin Fang heals her off every poisoned tick — buy Grievous Wounds before you commit.
